title: Finite etale covers and morphisms descend to finite subextensions
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $L/K$ a separable algebraic extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every intermediate field $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$ with $[E:K]<\infty$, put $X_E=X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}E$, and put $X_L=X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Finite etale covers and their morphisms mean [def-galois-categories].

(1) For every finite etale cover $P\to X_L$ there are such a field $E$, a finite etale cover $P_E\to X_E$, and an isomorphism $P_E\times_{X_E}X_L\cong P$ over $X_L$.

(2) If $P_E,Q_E$ are finite etale covers of $X_E$ and $f:P_E\times_{X_E}X_L\to Q_E\times_{X_E}X_L$ is any $X_L$-morphism, there is a finite intermediate field $E'$ containing $E$ and an $X_{E'}$-morphism $f_{E'}:P_E\times_{X_E}X_{E'}\to Q_E\times_{X_E}X_{E'}$ whose base change is $f$.

(3) If two $X_E$-morphisms $f_E,h_E:P_E\to Q_E$ have equal base changes to $X_L$, their base changes to $X_{E'}$ agree for some finite intermediate field $E'$ containing $E$.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit: equivalence of the filtered colimit of finite-etale cover categories with the cover category of the limit; specialized to X_E over finite intermediate fields of a separable algebraic extension. Objects, morphisms and eventual equality are the explicit meaning of this categorical equivalence.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finite intermediate fields of $L/K$, ordered by inclusion, with $K$ as its least element. Use the finite-subextension filtered-colimit presentation of [lem-kun-algebraic-separable-smooth]: the stages are the finite separable subextensions inside $L$. Thus $I$ is nonempty and directed and the inclusions give $L=\varinjlim_{E\in I}E$. The indexing collection is a set, being a subset of the power set of the underlying set of $L$; no large category is involved.

source.place: Statement and proof: finite separable subextensions and their filtered union

proof.text: For $E\in I$, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes $X_E$ separated and of finite type over $E$; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] then makes $X_E$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The same assertions hold for $X_L$. For $E\subseteq E'$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}E'\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is affine: the target spectrum of a field has only the empty open and the whole space, and their inverse images are affine. Its base change $X_{E'}\to X_E$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit], the inclusions $E\to L$ exhibit $\operatorname{Spec}L=\varprojlim_E\operatorname{Spec}E$. We check directly that $X_L$ with its canonical projections is the limit of the $X_E$. A compatible family $T\to X_E$ has one common component $T\to X_0$ (use the least stage $E=K$) and a compatible family $T\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, hence a unique component $T\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The two components agree over $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives exactly one $T\to X_L$ inducing the family. This proves the required limiting-cone assertion, including its specified projections.

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; Tag 01YZ, lemma-scheme-over-limit: verification by the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: Every finite etale cover $R\to Y$ used here, with $Y=X_E$ or $X_L$, is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since it is also finite, [lem-trf-finite-morphism-finite-presentation] makes it of finite presentation. In particular the spreading-out theorem applies both to the cover $P\to X_L$ in (1) and to the two covers $P_E,Q_E\to X_E$ in (2) and (3).

source.place: Tag 02GI, definition-etale; Tag 01S7, lemma-affine-separated; Tag 01TP, definition-finite-presentation

proof.text: Apply the object clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $P\to X_L$ and the system of steps 1--3. It gives $E_0\in I$, a finite-presentation morphism $p_0:R_0\to X_{E_0}$ and an isomorphism $R_0\times_{X_{E_0}}X_L\cong P$ over $X_L$. The source $R_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $p_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $X_{E_0}$ is qcqs. These are the absolute qcqs hypotheses required by the property-descent lemmas, not an assertion that $R_0$ is already finite or etale.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (1), followed by Situation 081D, situation-descent-property

proof.text: Restrict the directed system to $E\supseteq E_0$, still with limit $X_L$: the universal-property argument of step 3 works on this tail because every element of $L$ is in a finite subextension containing $E_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] with base system $S_E=X_E$, source $R_0$, target $X_{E_0}$ and morphism $p_0$. Its limit morphism is isomorphic to the finite morphism $P\to X_L$. The stage morphism is locally of finite type, since it is locally of finite presentation (a finitely presented algebra has finitely many generators). Hence some $E_1\supseteq E_0$ makes $p_1:R_1=R_0\times_{X_{E_0}}X_{E_1}\to X_{E_1}$ finite. Its finite presentation persists by part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and its source is qcqs by part (2).

source.place: Tag 01ZO, lemma-descend-finite-finite-presentation, in Situation 081D; morphisms.tex Tag 01TS, lemma-base-change-finite-presentation

proof.text: On the tail $E\supseteq E_1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] to $p_1$: the stage base, source and target are qcqs, the stage morphism is locally of finite presentation, and its limit morphism is $P\to X_L$, which is etale. It gives $E_2\supseteq E_1$ for which $p_2:R_2=R_1\times_{X_{E_1}}X_{E_2}\to X_{E_2}$ is etale. It remains finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a), applied to $p_1$. Consequently $P_{E_2}=R_2$ is a finite etale cover. The successive fibre-product universal properties identify its pullback to $X_L$ with $R_0\times_{X_{E_0}}X_L$, and the isomorphism of step 5 identifies this with $P$. This proves (1).

source.place: Tag 07RP, lemma-descend-etale, in Situation 081D; morphisms.tex Tag 01WL, lemma-base-change-finite

proof.text: For (2), apply the morphism clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out] at the specified index $E$, with $V_E=P_E$, $W_E=Q_E$ and $\psi=f$. These two schemes are of finite presentation over $X_E$ by step 4. We obtain $E'\supseteq E$ in $I$ and an $X_{E'}$-morphism between their pullbacks whose pullback to $X_L$ is $f$. The associativity identifications here are the unique ones preserving both fibre-product projections, so the domain and codomain are exactly the two covers specified in (2).

For (3), the covers $P_E,Q_E$ again have finite presentation by step 4. Apply the equality clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the two given $X_E$-morphisms $f_E,h_E$ and their assumed equal pullbacks to $X_L$. It gives an index $E'\supseteq E$ at which their pullbacks agree. Since indices are precisely finite intermediate fields of $L/K$, this is exactly the assertion of (3).
